newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soybeans close lower on technicals, funds.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soybeans close lower on technicals, funds.

text.p: CBOT soybeans closed lower on technical and fund selling with Refco Inc said a seller of at least 20 million bushels, 10 million in the November, traders said.
"Technically the market stinks. We took out support and down we went and there was big fund selling by Refco," said Vic Lespinasse of Dean Witter Reynolds. "It's still a seasonal downtrend."
Soybeans dropped despite a strong bean number in USDA's weekly export sales report, traders said.
"Exports and weather were both friendly," Lespinasse said.

USDA early Friday said U.S. soybean sales for the week ended October 10 totaled 1,163,700 tonnes, the largest weekly total in nearly eight years. The data included 100,000 tonnes to China and 256,900 tonnes to unknown. Some traders said the unknown tally may eventually be earmarked for China.
Soy was underpinned by a less-than-stellar outlook for soybean harvest weather in the U.S. Midwest.
Rain and cold temperatures are likely to slow the progress of corn and soybean harvests, meteorologists said.
Soybeans closed six to 7-1/4 cents per bushel lower, with November down 6-1/2 at $6.82.

"The first three days of the week were nearly ideal for harvesting and they (farmers) could have got a lot done. But beginning yesterday (Thursday) and looking into next week it doesn't look very good," agricultural meteorologist Joel Burgio of Weather Services Corp said.
Continental Grain again sold soybeans with nearly three million bushels sold in new crop November, traders said.
Continental also was a key seller of November soy during Thursday's session, from 10.0 to 15.0 million bushels, which led to talk China may have cancelled orders for U.S. soybeans.
"We keep hearing of business (China) but then the floor hears of defaults so it's pretty tough to trade," said Ron Kucha of O'Connor and Co.

Technical indicators before Friday's open confirmed there was little momentum in the market with first resistance in the November at $6.91-1/4 a bushel and second resistance at $6.97-3/4. The session high for November was $6.93-1/2 set near the open.

First support in November was at $6.84-3/4 and second support at $6.78-1/4, slightly above the session low of $6.77-1/2. The relative strength index (RSI) closed at 15.7 points, up from the close Thursday at 12.02 points. An RSI of 20 or less is generally considered indicative of an oversold market.
The four and 20 day moving averages continued to give off bearish chart signals.
"We're still stuck in a range with support in the low 80's," said Vic Lespinasse of Dean Witter Reynolds.
But one technical trader said Friday's performance indicated the soybean market may soon break out of the 20 cent range which was set recently between $6.80 and $7.00 per bushel.

"It was an outside day today, higher highs and higher lows and that means something is coming," a trader said. "Within the next three days it will probably either break out and go up or go even lower."
Soybean futures volume was estimated at 85,000, up from 68,554 Thursday, according to the CBOT.

Soybean options trading featured The Chicago Corp's sale of 750 January $6.75 puts at 9-1/2 cents and sale of 250 January $7.00 puts at 22 cents, traders said. First American bought 200 January $7.25 calls at 7-1/4 to 7-1/2 cents, they said.
Soybean options volume was estimated at 25,000, up from 21,823 Thursday.
